question: A complete breast examination includes palpation of the breast in both sitting and supine positions, as well as examination of both axillae and both supraclavicular fossae for lymphadenopathy.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. Breast examination is not limited to palpating the breast tissue. Both axillae and supraclavicular fossae must be examined for lymphadenopathy, and examining in both sitting and supine positions ensures complete coverage of the breast parenchyma.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. A thorough breast examination is systematic: inspection (sitting, arms raised and pressed on hips), palpation (sitting then supine with ipsilateral arm raised), followed by lymph node examination of both axillae and the supraclavicular fossae — all nodes that drain breast tissue.
